C047-N3.title: Explorers cannot renew their availability after their published dates expire

checks.reason: Expired availability posts disappear from the feed that the editor uses to find the user's existing post. The editor therefore submits a create request, which the explorer one-post check rejects even when the previous post has expired. Delete Pitch also requires the missing existingPostId; direct API editing remains possible, but this screen provides no recovery.

The web editor finds 'mine' only among the posts returned by /feed. That feed drops posts whose latest availability date has passed (is_talent_board_visible), so existingPostId stays null. Saving then calls createExplorerPost, and _create_newcomer_post rejects it because any ExplorerPost from this explorer still exists. The delete button returns early when existingPostId is null, so Zoe cannot get out of this state from the UI.

C028-N4.title: Overnight attendance corrections leave the next period approved with stale minutes

checks.reason: Attendance corrections invalidate only periods containing the session's original local clock-in date, although attendance calculations include and clip sessions across period boundaries. The Monday period therefore keeps its old minutes, approval, and false needs_rebuild flag. Neither opening its detail nor locking it checks the source fingerprint again, so the stale approved period can be locked.

Every attendance signal calls _enqueue with _session_date(session), the local date of started_at. Only the period containing the clock-in is marked needs_rebuild. _session_rows clips each session to the period bounds, so Monday's period does include the overnight minutes, but nothing marks it stale after Monday's clock-out is corrected. The attendance app has no other rebuild trigger. lock_period checks only needs_rebuild and APPROVED status, so the next period locks with the old minutes.

C028-N5.title: Archiving a roster removes its scheduled work and approved leave from timesheets

checks.reason: An authorized manager can archive a published roster without first locking its timesheets, and saving the archived status invalidates overlapping unlocked timesheets. Rebuilding excludes that week's assignments because roster inputs require PUBLISHED status, so scheduled minutes and leave minutes derived from those assignments disappear. Approved leave records remain approved, while the worker roster explicitly retains archived weeks as published history.

Archiving can be called from v2_views and has no time check. The status save fires roster_period_changed, which rebuilds every timesheet in the matching unlocked periods. _roster_rows keeps only weeks with status PUBLISHED, so an archived week contributes no roster rows. Approved-leave minutes are counted only where leave overlaps roster rows, so both rostered and leave minutes fall to zero, and an approved timesheet moves to REOPENED. Meanwhile get_worker_published_roster still treats ARCHIVED as published history.

C038-N1.title: Post-verification and dashboard return links navigate to an unrouted root path, landing users on a 404 page

checks.reason: The cited links reach the wildcard 404 when served by Vite without the public-site handoff, including the production routing configuration with PUBLIC_SITE_ENABLED disabled. The broader claim overlooks the Next /dashboard account gate, staging's explicit routing to that gate, and Vite's optional cross-origin bridge. This is a conditional P2 navigation defect in the standalone or rollback configuration, rather than a universal onboarding failure.

C016-N2.title: Hub group PATCH can reassign an existing group to an unrelated pharmacy without checking destination tenant authority.

checks.reason: 'pharmacy' is in HubCommunityGroupSerializer.Meta.read_only_fields, so DRF drops any pharmacy value sent in a PATCH. perform_update calls serializer.save() with no pharmacy argument. The group cannot be moved to another pharmacy through this endpoint.

F13-N1.title: A Hub with more than 50 posts repeatedly clears and reloads its mobile feed.

checks.reason: The `load` callback lists `next` as a dependency, and the mount effect depends on `load`. So when a page comes back with a non-null `next` (DRF PageNumberPagination, PAGE_SIZE 50, which HubPostViewSet.list uses), `load` is rebuilt and the effect runs again. Each run clears posts, the open discussion, the comment draft and the reply target, sets `next` back to null (which rebuilds `load` again) and fetches again, so it loops for as long as the Hub has more than 50 posts. Load more is also broken: it calls `fetchHubPosts(nextUrl)`, so the URL string is passed as the scope argument and `options.cursor` is never set. `buildScopeParams` then reads `scope.type` from a string, gets undefined, and sends a request with no valid scope instead of following the next URL.

C048-N1.title: Correcting a poll question silently deletes every existing vote.

checks.reason: The web poll dialog always sends the full options list with the question, and updateHubPollService passes it on. The backend's update turns `options` into `option_labels`. Whenever `option_labels` is present, the serializer deletes every PharmacyHubPollVote and every option and recreates them, without checking whether the labels changed. So editing only the question silently wipes all votes; the dialog shows no warning. This is real, but the lost data is informal Hub poll votes, so P2 rather than P1.

C077-N1.title: Referee decline links do not match the web page or its request

checks.reason: The email builds the decline link as `/onboarding/referee-reject/{token}`, which is one path segment; the signed token contains colons but no slash. The Next page and the old SPA route both need two segments (`/:pk/:refIndex`), so the link matches no page. Even if a page rendered, it calls the deprecated `refereeReject(pk, refIndex)` endpoint, which POSTs to `/onboarding/referee-reject/{pk}/{refIndex}/`. Django only routes `onboarding/referee-reject/<str:token>/`, and the existing token client (`refereeRejectByToken`) is never used. The decline is never recorded, so the reference stays pending and reminders keep going.

C077-N2.title: Expired availability prevents Explorers from publishing again

checks.reason: The web Talent Board finds the user's own post only in `useTalentFeed`, which calls the `feed` action. That action drops posts that fail `is_talent_board_visible`, which includes dated availability whose last date has passed. So for an expired post `existingPostId` stays null: the form offers neither edit nor delete and submits a create. For an Explorer, `_create_newcomer_post` refuses any create while any of their posts exists, expired or not, with "Edit it, or delete it to post again", which the UI cannot do. No backend job removes expired posts; the only delete happens on role upgrade.

F14-U8.title: Workers can clock in only with the counter QR or kiosk PIN; there is no manual fallback when both are unavailable.

checks.reason: Worker clock-in requires a valid pharmacy QR token, while kiosk alternatives require a working kiosk. Missing-punch and manager-correction workflows require an existing session or event, so they cannot create Sara's initial attendance record when neither clocking method is available. Choosing an alternative form of attendance evidence requires an owner policy decision.

F14-U2.title: The marketplace listing gate lists 'Verify your mobile number' with no way to do it, and the 8-step bar is cut off at desktop width.

checks.reason: The mobile-verification blocker is returned for an unverified owner, but the gate renders links only for identity and onboarding blockers. This confirms a missing route from the mobile prerequisite to its completion screen, rather than a complete inability to verify a mobile number. Terms can be accepted directly below the list, and the step bar allows horizontal scrolling; permanent label truncation at 1440px is not established by source alone.

F14-U4.title: Ethical marketplace sub-pages keep the generic landing page title, so browser tabs and history cannot be told apart.

checks.reason: Inventory, listings and transfers render different workspace views but export no page title. Their shared ethical layout supplies only robots metadata, and the workspace does not update document.title. All three therefore inherit the same generic title from the root layout, including when access prerequisites are unmet.

F14-U6.title: Typing a date (DD/MM/YYYY) in the post-shift date field is rejected with 'Pick a date first'; only the picker works.

checks.reason: The date picker explicitly uses DD/MM/YYYY and stores any valid value supplied by its onChange callback, without distinguishing typing from calendar selection. Add date reports 'Pick a date first' only when that stored value is empty. Whether keyboard entry fails to produce a valid callback depends on the rendered picker interaction; the supplied screenshot shows an empty field and does not settle that.

F14-U1.title: The public shift board offers Apply Now on shifts for a role the worker cannot take, then shows only a vague failure toast.

checks.reason: The public listing includes all roles, and Apply Now checks verification without checking whether the worker can perform that role. The application endpoint excludes technician shifts from a pharmacist's queryset and returns 404. The page replaces that response with the reported generic failure message, so the backend guard prevents the application but does not prevent the confusing UI.

F14-U3.title: Several phone tap targets are below 44px (public job board map/report buttons, talent board nav links, landing role pills, dashboard top-bar icons).

checks.reason: Confirmed at P2 for the small map IconButton, 32px Report target, 36px landing role pills and explicitly 38px phone dashboard icons. The later landing CSS overrides the earlier 44px minimum. The broader claim about talent-board navigation is not established: the mobile menu links receive 12px padding on each side, and account-menu entries have a 44px minimum.

F14-U5.title: On phone, tapping the 'I agree to the Terms' label may open the terms link instead of ticking the box, leaving Register disabled.

checks.reason: The form uses FormControlLabel with a controlled Checkbox whose onChange updates acceptedTerms, so ordinary label text activates the checkbox. Only the policy names are links, with target="_blank"; neither the navigation wrapper nor the surrounding styles extend them over the other label text. Opening a policy by tapping its linked words is expected behavior and does not establish the claimed registration blocker.

F14-U7.title: If the API cannot be reached at start-up, the web app shows an unstyled error with run-together buttons; Reconnect reloads into the same state and Retry logout has no way out.

checks.reason: Confirmed at P2 for the Vite application: a startup identity-request failure replaces the router with adjacent plain buttons without spacing or target sizing. Reconnect reloads the same bootstrap, while failed logout returns to the error without clearing local authentication. The scope is narrower than the whole website because Next public pages retain their separate header and footer outside the migrated authentication provider.

C073-N1.title: The publishing workspace leaves private content visible after logout

checks.reason: The /content layout shows PublicHeader, which contains AccountControls. Its Log out button calls logoutSession(), and that function only POSTs the logout, clears browser storage and announces the event. It does not redirect. ContentDashboard loads `me`, `rows`, `doc` and `form` once and never reads useSession or watchSession, so the open draft and the publish controls stay on screen after logout. This is real, but it only shows text that was already on the screen to someone using the same browser tab. Any later save, publish or list call needs the cleared session and fails, so it is a shared-device problem, not a cross-account data leak. P2.

C078-N2.title: Editing a shift silently replaces custom date rates with calculated rates

checks.reason: When the editor loads a shift, it fills slotRateRows from the saved per-date rates and marks each row dirty:false. Setting the slots changes expandedSlots, and that runs the reconcile effect with previous=[], which resets every row to empty. It also starts calculateShiftRates, which overwrites any row whose dirty flag is not set with the rate worked out from the guide rate (the form's rate_weekday and similar fields). buildShiftDraftSlotPayload then sends that calculated rate, and revise_shift deletes the old slots and recreates them with it. So a saved $80 date becomes $60 when only the description was edited. If the pricing call fails, the rate is saved as null instead.

C078-N3.title: Saving a partially filled shift can delete its confirmed bookings

checks.reason: The editor loads the shift from /shifts/active/{id}/. get_slots on that endpoint drops every (slot, date) pair that already has an assignment, so the form only knows about the open date. On save, the PATCH to /shifts/{id}/ (ShiftDetailViewSet, which has no update override; the only check is manage-pharmacy) sends the slots list. revise_shift then runs instance.slots.all().delete(), and its only refusal is for roster slots or rostered assignments. ShiftSlotAssignment.slot is on_delete=CASCADE, and the pre_delete signal only acts on rostered assignments, so Sara's marketplace booking is deleted without a cancellation flow. The Edit button on ActiveShiftCard is shown with no condition.

B01.title: Subscriber discount omitted from shift checkout

checks.reason: charge_shift_fulfillment works out is_subscriber (active OwnerSubscription) but never uses it. price_id is always the standard locum ($30) or PT/FT ($80) price. The comments list the subscriber price IDs ($15/$40), and the pricing pages promise subscribers 50% off fulfilment fees. No test checks which Stripe price is used, so active subscribers are charged full price.

B04.title: Empty and duplicate shift checkout sessions possible

checks.reason: When no offer_ids or slot_ids are sent, there is no check that any offer is ACCEPTED_AWAITING_PAYMENT, and quantity becomes max(1,0)=1. The shared-core client says the existing callers send a bodyless POST, so this is the normal UI path. Paying finalizes every pending offer for one unit, and a shift with nothing pending still gets a payable session. Nothing stops duplicate sessions: no Stripe idempotency key and no lookup for an open session or payment. The webhook dedupes by event id only and creates a new ShiftPayment for every paid session, even when nothing is finalized.

B10.title: Multi-offer Pills spend uses one shift-wide ledger key; concurrency risk

checks.reason: pay_shift calls spend_pills_for_shift_post once per unit, but every call uses the same key f"shift:{shift.id}:pill-payment". _create_ledger_entry returns the existing row when that key is found, so only one unit is ever deducted. Because the key is shift-wide, a later payment on the same shift (still PENDING after a partial payment) is free. Separately, the balance is read with no select_for_update, so two concurrent spends on different shifts can both pass. The finalize step also runs in its own transaction, after the spend. This is a deterministic undercharge, not just a concurrency risk.

B14.title: Legacy casual award figures and incomplete future holiday data

checks.reason: public_holidays.json lists 2026 dates only, and is_public_holiday is an exact string lookup. Any slot from 1 Jan 2027 (New Year, Australia Day) is priced as a weekday by get_locked_rate_for_slot for award-priced non-pharmacist shifts, so the locked rate falls below the holiday rate. VIC also seems to be missing the 2026 AFL Grand Final eve. The 'legacy award figures' half cannot be settled from the code: the single unversioned casual table (e.g. Assistant L1 $33.19) has to be compared with the FWO MA000012 pay guide in force after 1 July 2026. Lowered to P1 because the rate is a suggested or locked figure, not a payment the platform makes.

B16.title: Pharmacy Admin update bypasses management privilege

checks.reason: PharmacyAdminViewSet is a plain ModelViewSet with no update or partial_update override and only IsAuthenticated. get_queryset lets an admin of any level (including COMMUNICATION_MANAGER) reach every assignment in their pharmacy. The serializer leaves user, pharmacy, membership, is_active and staff_role writable, and pharmacy accepts any Pharmacy id. Its validate() only checks for an existing duplicate and owner demotion. So a low-level admin can PATCH their own assignment's pharmacy to a foreign pharmacy and keep their level there, or re-activate or reassign other rows. The MANAGE_ADMINS check runs only in create() and destroy(), and no test covers PATCH or PUT.

B17.title: Chain update can attach foreign pharmacy and affect membership deletion

checks.reason: ChainSerializer.pharmacy_ids is a writable PrimaryKeyRelatedField over Pharmacy.objects.all(). Create, PUT and PATCH therefore skip the owner/organization match that add_pharmacy enforces. Any owner, or any org-wide admin of any organization, passes check_permissions and can attach a foreign pharmacy to their own chain. remove_user then deletes the first Membership of any user_id in any chain pharmacy, including the foreign one. Chain membership also widens shift escalation and rate visibility (candidates.py, lifecycle.py, rate_visibility.py), and the pharmacies action shows the foreign pharmacy's details.

B18.title: Claim PUT path bypasses owner approval workflow

checks.reason: The viewset mixes in UpdateModelMixin, so PUT goes to the inherited update() and skips the owner-only, PENDING-only checks in partial_update. The serializer leaves status, message and response_message writable. That means an admin of the requesting organization (who is in the queryset through full_org_ids) can PUT {"status":"ACCEPTED"} on their own claim with no owner approval. PUT never runs _accept_claim, so pharmacy.organization does not change and there is no real takeover. The damage is a fake ACCEPTED claim that appears in the org dashboard's accepted list and blocks other organizations from claiming (claims.py:315-323), a 500 if the unique constraint trips, and the ability to reopen REJECTED claims.

B19.title: Invite links can be retargeted; removal may cascade applications

checks.reason: MembershipInviteLinkViewSet is a plain ModelViewSet. Only create() checks user_can_invite_members_to_pharmacy, and the serializer leaves pharmacy, category, expires_at and is_active writable. So anyone who can see a link (owner, org scope or MANAGE_STAFF admin) can PATCH it to point at any other pharmacy, and new applications then go to that pharmacy (serializers.py:532, views.py:241,289-295). Deleting a link cascades its MembershipApplication rows (models.py:246). Neither PATCH nor DELETE is called by the shared-core client, and the target pharmacy's owner still has to approve each application, so this is an API-only integrity and spam problem, not P0.

B21.title: Cover request scope differs from assignment scope

checks.reason: The serializer accepts pharmacy and shift (a ShiftSlotAssignment) separately and never checks that the assignment belongs to that pharmacy, or that the requester is linked to that pharmacy at all. On approval, _assert_decider_permissions and release_worker_from_assignment check authority only on req.pharmacy. Then they delete req.shift and escalate the visibility of a shift that may belong to a different pharmacy or organization (pharmacy B). The only guard is that the requester must be the current assignee (worker_actions.py:359), so a worker can get their assignment at B released by a manager at A without B's consent. This needs a manager at A to approve, which is why it is P1 and not P0.

B22.title: Org poll aggregation includes private pharmacy polls

checks.reason: Polls created in pharmacy scope are saved with pharmacy=P1 and organization=P1.organization (access.py:214-216, serialization/polls.py:121-124). The organization list filter matches Q(organization=org) | Q(pharmacy__organization=org), so every pharmacy-private poll, with its votes and comments, appears in the org hub list. Anyone with a staff membership at any pharmacy in the org can see it, and so can a region admin scoped to other pharmacies (access.py:286-306). Direct retrieve is safe because it re-resolves scope from the poll (polls.py:129-131). The code comment at polls.py:84 shows this was deliberate and it differs from how posts are scoped (scoping.py:162-168), so the owner must decide whether it should change.

B23.title: Chief Admin may mutate/delete organization record

checks.reason: Update, partial_update and destroy on OrganizationViewSet use ORG_WIDE_ADMIN_ROLES. That list is built from VIEW_ALL_PHARMACIES, which CHIEF_ADMIN has, so a Chief Admin can edit or delete the organization record. The viewset docstring and the role definition both say Chief Admin is meant to share org-admin powers, so this matches the stated design. The open point is a policy conflict: deleting the whole organization goes further than the rule that a Chief Admin 'cannot create or change organisation admins'. The owner must decide; the code does nothing beyond what it says it does.

B24.title: Exchange action accepts confirm-completion while still in ENQUIRY / TERMS_PROPOSED, and arbitrary propose-terms/cancel/decline after accepted or completed; buyer can invoke decline. This bypasses accepted terms and reservation lifecycle.

checks.reason: Apart from accept, ExchangeAction checks only that the caller is a participant and that expected_version matches. It never checks the current state. Buyer or seller can decline, cancel or propose-terms from any state, including ACCEPTED and COMPLETED, and when both confirm-completion from ENQUIRY or TERMS_PROPOSED the exchange and listing become COMPLETED with no reservation or agreed terms. Nothing ever sets a MarketplaceReservation inactive, so cancelling after accept leaves the listing RESERVED for good. The steps are not atomic or locked either. There is no payment movement here and both parties must be participants, so this is P1 and not P0.

B29.title: Signed offline event integrity flags for clock-anchor drift, backward time, monotonic rollback and seven-day server drift mark evidence NEEDS_REVIEW but still call live attendance mutation, so suspect timestamps can create normal AttendanceSessions.

checks.reason: _integrity_flags adds CLOCK_MOVED_BACKWARDS, MONOTONIC_ROLLBACK, CLOCK_ANCHOR_DRIFT and SERVER_TIME_DRIFT, and any flag turns the status into NEEDS_REVIEW. But only SEQUENCE_GAP, HASH_CHAIN_MISMATCH, UNEXPECTED_INITIAL_HASH and DEVICE_REVOKED_DRAIN stop _apply_business_event. So the device timestamp still goes into clock_in/clock_out as occurred_at, with no time-sanity check in transitions.clock_in, and a normal AttendanceSession is created. Nothing outside protocol.py and models.py reads NEEDS_REVIEW or integrity_flags: no review queue exists and timesheets are not touched. I lowered it to P1 because it needs a paired, signing native kiosk whose clock is wrong or has been changed, and the flags are kept for audit.

B35.area: Roster-create cross-tenant writes: RosterOwnerViewSet is an authenticated ModelViewSet with pharmacy-filtered get_queryset but default create/perform_create; RosterA
B35.title: SOURCE-FINDING

checks.reason: RosterOwnerViewSet is a full ModelViewSet with only IsAuthenticated. get_queryset limits reads and object lookups to managed pharmacies, but create is the default one and is not checked. RosterAssignmentSerializer exposes writable user/slot/shift primary keys with no validate or create override, so any logged-in user can POST /roster-owner/ and create a ShiftSlotAssignment on any pharmacy's slot, for themselves or anyone else. The model save only checks the published-roster lock, and no test covers a cross-tenant POST. PATCH on an assignment the user may manage can also move it to a foreign shift or slot, because perform_update only checks the lock.

B54.title: P0-impact / P1 candidate — Two worker confirmations can reserve and pay for the same slot; a paid losing offer can appear ACCEPTED without an assignment

checks.reason: offer_shift only blocks a new offer when the slot already has an assignment or an ACCEPTED_AWAITING_PAYMENT offer, so several candidates can hold PENDING offers for the same slot. ShiftOfferViewSet.accept has no lock and never re-checks the slot. When payment is required, each acceptance becomes ACCEPTED_AWAITING_PAYMENT without expiring the others. This happens even one after another, with no race needed. Checkout only refuses two offers per slot inside one checkout. With two separate checkouts the owner pays twice and the second webhook finalizes nothing. A checkout by slot or with no filter makes finalize_shift_offer skip the slot that is already assigned and still mark the losing offer ACCEPTED with no assignment. On the free path the race is concurrent only: it either raises an IntegrityError from unique (slot, slot_date) or gives the same ACCEPTED offer with no assignment. I lowered it to P1 because the money lost is one placement fee, not a cross-tenant breach.

B46.title: P0/P1 candidate: Pending/left pharmacy memberships can access or author private pharmacy, group and organisation Hub content

checks.reason: Every Hub access path requires Membership.is_active=True: the pharmacy, group and organisation scopes, the hub context, groups and the directory. Pending invitations are created with is_active=False, and reject and quit set is_active=False along with REJECTED/LEFT, so pending, rejected and left members cannot read or post. ensure_author_membership no longer reactivates memberships for ordinary staff. The only leftover is a manager PATCHing is_active=True on a PENDING membership, since MembershipSerializer exposes both status and is_active as writable to managers. That is a manager's deliberate action, not a bypass, but adding status=ACCEPTED to the hub filters, as directory.py already does, would close it.

B02.title: Purchased extra seats cannot subsequently be adjusted

checks.reason: Successful extra-seat checkout stores stripe_extra_seat_subscription_id, after which the seat endpoint rejects every further quantity change. The billing screen still offers quantity changes and submits them to that endpoint. Billing permissions restrict who can submit, but do not provide an alternative adjustment flow.

B08.title: Region Admin notified about unrelated pharmacy shifts

checks.reason: Manager notifications include every active Region Admin belonging to the shift pharmacy's organization, without checking assigned pharmacies. A real interest submission reaches this helper, and notification delivery checks account activity but does not enforce pharmacy scope. The exposure concerns other pharmacies within the same organization; the separate shift-access guard does not prevent receiving the notification contents.

B11.title: Abandoned payments can indefinitely reserve slots

checks.reason: Worker acceptance under payment-required billing changes the offer to ACCEPTED_AWAITING_PAYMENT. Slot locking treats that status as reserved without checking expires_at, while automatic expiry handles only PENDING offers and the webhook ignores checkout expiry events. Abandoning payment therefore leaves the reservation without an automatic release deadline; the owner must choose the payment grace period and late-payment policy.

B13.title: Account deletion leaves future booked shifts without handover

checks.reason: The authenticated deletion endpoint deactivates and anonymizes the user without checking future assignments, releasing bookings, or notifying their managers. Assignments retain their user foreign key because the user row is saved rather than deleted, so those slots remain occupied. Existing deletion tests cover identity cleanup and token revocation, not booked shifts; the owner must choose whether deletion blocks, cancels, or initiates a handover.

B25.title: ListingAudience saves current circle and bumps listing.version before validating every requested schedule item. Invalid later schedule returns 400 after persistent state mutation.

checks.reason: An authorized listing owner can submit valid circles and a schedule whose later entry exceeds the maximum. The handler saves the audience and listing version, and creates earlier schedule entries, before raising the schedule validation error. Neither the handler nor database settings wrap the request in a transaction, and the audience signal validates only the audience fields, so those earlier writes persist despite the 400 response.

B27.title: TimesheetPeriod creation rejects inverted/overlong date ranges but allows overlapping ranges for same pharmacy, while payroll manifests can each represent the same attendance/roster minutes.

checks.reason: Period creation validates date order and length but checks uniqueness only for identical pharmacy/date tuples, allowing intersecting windows. Each period independently selects the same dated assignments and attendance, and locking checks approval within that period without excluding evidence exported in another manifest. The web screen can create overlapping fortnights on successive weeks; duplicate exported evidence is established, but automatic duplicate payment is not. The owner must choose whether to prohibit overlapping payroll periods or deduplicate their payable evidence.

B30.title: Established notification WebSocket stays subscribed to user group after logout, user deactivation or credential revocation; consumer sends notification and message badge events without checking current account/session eligibility.

checks.reason: A separately maintained notification socket remains subscribed after logout or credential revocation because authentication runs only at connection time and logout sends no disconnect event. The deactivation claim is narrower: notification creation and chat badge producers filter inactive users, and the web client closes its own socket during local logout. Those guards do not stop delivery to a retained socket for an active account whose credentials were revoked.

B32.title: The signed kiosk event field is named shift_id but is forwarded as assignment_id; an explicitly supplied ID shortcut accepts an assignment regardless of event-date shift window, potentially linking old assignments as current attendance.

checks.reason: A valid signed kiosk CLOCK_IN forwards shift_id directly as assignment_id. Explicit assignment lookup checks worker, pharmacy and draft status, then returns before checking the event's date or shift window. A current event naming that worker's old non-draft assignment therefore creates a non-provisional session linked to it; neither event storage nor session constraints reject this mismatch.

B37.area: Worker roster disclosure: RosterWorkerViewSet.get_queryset includes all assignments in pharmacies with is_active membership, but does not require status ACC
B37.title: SOURCE-FINDING

checks.reason: The authenticated roster endpoint grants pharmacy-wide assignment visibility from is_active alone, without requiring ACCEPTED membership or excluding CONTACT. Membership updates can independently change status and activity, and no database constraint enforces their consistency. Draft and unpublished filters limit which assignments appear, while the serializer's workforce-status guard hides timesheet details but still exposes other workers' emails and unit rates.

B39.area: Rate default destructive update: sync_pharmacy_rate_defaults sets six pharmacy rate fields to None when apply_rates_to_pharmacy is true but caller omits those fiel
B39.title: SOURCE-FINDING

checks.reason: An authorized pharmacist-shift edit with apply_rates_to_pharmacy=true and omitted rate fields reaches the helper, which converts every omission to None and saves all six defaults. No serializer check requires a complete rate payload. This is P2 because it requires explicit opt-in and changes pharmacy defaults rather than existing assignment rates; ordinary edits default the flag to false, and the current web save-defaults action uses a separate pharmacy update.

B52.title: P1 candidate — Expo startup trusts cached identity and role after server rejects or cannot verify account, unlike web

checks.reason: Mobile bootstrap swallows identity-request failures and restores the saved user and role when stored credentials remain, allowing AuthGate to retain role-based navigation after a connection failure or an unhandled 403. However, a 401 followed by failed refresh clears storage, and a successful identity response replaces the cached user. The confirmed impact is stale signed-in UI, rated P2; this path does not establish access to server-protected data.

B55.title: P1 candidate — Concurrent approval of *unlinked* cover request publishes multiple paid vacancies

checks.reason: Two authorized approvals can both load the same unlinked PENDING request before either saves its new status. Each then creates a separate locum Shift and ShiftSlot, with no locked request recheck or uniqueness constraint tying the vacancy to its originating request. The linked-assignment branch has locking, but that protection is bypassed here; approval publishes duplicate vacancies rather than itself charging payment.

B57.title: P1 conditional — Refund provider events are acknowledged without reversing/reconciling local paid financial state

checks.reason: A signed refund event falls through the dispatcher and is still marked processed with HTTP 200. The original ShiftPayment and shift payment status remain paid, with no refund reconciliation path found. This confirms stale financial state after a refund; it does not imply that the worker's assignment should automatically be cancelled.

B59.title: P1 conditional — Revisions can reduce payable below recorded payments, producing negative balance

checks.reason: An invoice owner can revise payable from 880 to 100 after recording an 880 payment: revision validation checks positivity but never compares existing payments. Payments remain attached, and serialization returns a balance of -780, which the document uses as the amount due. P2 because this is an owner-controlled correction with preserved history; the owner must decide whether to reject such revisions or represent an overpayment and its reconciliation explicitly.

B61.title: P1 user-facing accuracy candidate — Expo payroll CSV exports blanks for fields absent from the timesheet API

checks.reason: The mobile export directly reads hours and pay fields that neither the timesheet serializer nor its shared contract supplies, including every fallback name. An approved timesheet therefore produces four empty numeric columns despite having worked_minutes. P2 because the exported file is incomplete; this path does not itself calculate or submit incorrect wages.

B63.title: P1 conditional — Native-kiosk pairing authorization can be redeemed as web-online by declaring a non-native platform

checks.reason: Issued authorizations specify NATIVE_OFFLINE, but an empty or non-native platform skips signing proof and the allowed-client-kind check, creating a WEB_ONLINE device. This is narrower than an offline security bypass: valid unexpired code possession and manager authorization remain required, and offline sync rejects web devices. P2 and a policy decision because the web client and existing tests deliberately support this redemption flow.

B65.title: P1 scoped-information candidate — Authenticated pricing-preview endpoint lets unrelated users derive private pharmacy guide rates

checks.reason: The calculator requires authentication but bypasses pharmacy-management checks and loads the submitted pharmacy ID directly. A pharmacist FLEXIBLE preview without overrides returns that pharmacy's configured day rate, including to staff whose normal shift responses deliberately remove those defaults. P2 because the demonstrated disclosure concerns pharmacy guide rates, rather than individual wages or agreed assignment terms.

B42.title: P1 candidate — Marketplace draft PATCH returns error after partial persistence

checks.reason: An authorized draft owner can submit a valid title/audience edit with delivery known_cost='1.001': the dictionary validation accepts it, then delivery full_clean rejects its decimal precision after the listing and audience have saved. Neither the PATCH path nor database configuration supplies a surrounding transaction, so those earlier writes persist. P2 because this affects owned drafts/rejected listings; the unhandled Django validation error also means the claimed 400 is not assured.

B45.title: P1 candidate — Incomplete referee questionnaire can be counted as a verified reference

checks.reason: A referee with a valid, unused signed link can omit would_rehire because the model allows blank values and the serializer adds no required-answer validation. The submission handler marks every answer except 'no' as confirmed, and verification policy counts both confirmed flags as verified referees. Token and duplicate-submission checks do not prevent an incomplete first submission; the existing response-validation test covers duplicates only.

B48.title: P1 candidate: Pharmacy Hub mention validation can deliver confidential private post text to ineligible locum or non-accepted members

checks.reason: An authorized author can supply an active same-pharmacy locum membership ID directly, although the directory hides locums and the Hub access resolver denies them access. Mention delivery checks account activity but never checks the recipient's Hub access, storing a 280-character body preview and queuing the full body for email. The non-accepted staff case overlaps B46's permissive Hub access, but the locum notification leak independently confirms this finding. Existing tests cover locum read denial and eligible-recipient notifications, not rejection of ineligible mention IDs.

B50.title: P1 candidate — Active but non-accepted pharmacy membership can read community-chat last-message previews

checks.reason: The authenticated room list includes pharmacy community rooms for active staff memberships without checking accepted status or participation, and its serializer returns the latest message's first 200 characters. This state is reachable: an authorized manager can activate a pending membership through generic PATCH without changing its status. The participant check protects the separate messages action only; existing community-chat tests do not cover previews for active pending members.

B67.title: P1 booking/financial-evidence candidate: generic shift-offer DELETE bypasses state-machine transitions

checks.reason: The routed viewset exposes default DELETE to the offer's worker or a permitted pharmacy manager without a status check or custom deletion handler. Payment-required acceptance saves ACCEPTED_AWAITING_PAYMENT without creating an assignment, so assignment-level PROTECT does not stop deletion of that offer and its accepted terms. This bypasses the pending-only decline transition and removes the row billing uses for finalization; it does not establish deletion of an already booked assignment. Existing offer characterization tests cover visibility and blocked creation, not DELETE.

B05.title: Already-connected sockets may outlive access revocation

checks.reason: An accepted pharmacy participant can connect, then lose membership access while the socket remains subscribed. The membership signal deletes the Participant row but does not disconnect existing sockets; outbound messages recheck only AHPRA suspension. Room broadcasts therefore still deliver new messages to that connection.

B09.title: Shift escalation depends on reads and omits audience notification

checks.reason: Automatic shift escalation is called from BaseShiftViewSet.get_queryset, with no scheduled caller registered for this function. Without a qualifying request, a due shift retains its old audience. Both automatic and manual escalation save visibility without notifying the newly eligible audience; the Shift save signal only updates roster revisions.

B12.title: Rating can be submitted before completed work

checks.reason: Both rating creation branches treat any assignment at the relevant pharmacy as a completed relationship, including a future booking. The pending-ratings endpoint filters for past dates, but creation does not apply that restriction. Serializer and model validation check rating shape, stars and uniqueness, without checking completed work.

B20.title: Interest/rejection mutation can target a different shift

checks.reason: An authenticated worker can PATCH an interest or rejection they already own and change its shift to another existing shift. The queryset authorizes access to the original row, while both serializers leave shift writable and provide no reassignment validation. Neither model adds a guard, so destination audience and application rules are bypassed.

B26.title: EthicalListing draft is persisted before checking lot selection, lot ownership and available quantities; invalid listing create can leave orphan or partially allocated regulated-stock drafts.

checks.reason: An otherwise authorized request saves the draft before rejecting missing lots, an existing foreign lot, or quantity exceeding availability. A valid first allocation also remains when a later allocation fails these checks, because the request has no enclosing transaction. P2: this leaves incomplete drafts and allocation rows, without reserving or deducting stock; nonexistent lot IDs are rejected earlier by nested serializer validation.

B28.title: Timesheet check decision path allows new resolved/waived decision on a check belonging to an already LOCKED period without correction/reopen process.

checks.reason: A pharmacy manager can resolve or waive an eligible check after its period is LOCKED: neither the endpoint nor decide_check checks period status. This changes the displayed decision and effective warning counts, without changing the frozen payroll snapshot or manifest hash. P2: the demonstrated impact is post-lock review metadata; the owner must decide whether these recorded annotations are allowed or must require the correction workflow.

B31.title: Ethical listing request verifies PUBLISHED status before transaction but never locks/rechecks listing inside it; two concurrent requests can create two active transfers for one single-reservation listing if they reserve different available lots.

checks.reason: When ethical transfers are enabled, two requests can both read PUBLISHED before either transaction reserves the listing. Each transaction locks only its selected lots, then creates a transfer and writes RESERVED without rechecking listing status. Distinct lots and request IDs avoid the existing stock and receipt constraints; no constraint limits active transfers per listing. The feature is disabled by default.

B34.title: ExplorerPostViewSet feed and public-feed filter is_talent_board_visible (moderator hidden and expired), but generic retrieve, list and by-profile/raw view/like handlers inherit an unrestricted queryset; a hidden post can remain readable/reactable by ID and via list.

checks.reason: Authenticated list, retrieve, view and like requests use the unrestricted queryset, so moderator-hidden posts remain readable and reactable through those routes. Authentication is their only relevant permission, and serialization does not suppress hidden posts. The claim is narrower than reported because by-profile explicitly applies the visibility filter; an existing test also documents that plain list includes expired posts.

B38.area: Roster assignment overwrite: RosterShiftManageViewSet.update explicitly permits user_id to update_or_create each ShiftSlotAssignment after serializer update; i
B38.title: SOURCE-FINDING

checks.reason: Normal editor requests include slots and enter the guarded in-place editor, which rejects reassignment of invoice-linked assignments. However, a managing user can omit slots and PATCH only user_id after unpublishing the affected shift. That path updates the existing assignment's worker and terms without checking invoice or attendance history; the model guard checks publication status only. The existing invoice regression test covers the guarded slots payload, leaving this alternate payload reachable.

B40.area: Booking eligibility stale verification: onboarding verification evaluate preserves was_verified when base checks are missing except for specified AHPRA adverse states; th
B40.title: SOURCE-FINDING

checks.reason: An already-verified worker can resend a mobile OTP, which clears is_mobile_verified without clearing profile.verified; public shift applications still trust the saved profile flag. Marketplace access and staff talent posting independently check mobile verification, so those cited paths do not share the bypass. Preserving verification when base checks are missing is explicitly documented owner policy and covered by a test. Whether requesting another OTP should suspend public booking eligibility is therefore a policy decision, rather than an established P1 authorization defect.

B53.title: P1 candidate — Out-of-order Stripe subscription events may reactivate cancelled base billing or reset purchased seat entitlement

checks.reason: A base subscription deletion sets the local account inactive, but a later invoice.paid for its tracked add-on sets that same account active without checking the base subscription. A delayed base checkout completion also resets staff_count to five even when an add-on is already recorded. Webhook deduplication protects individual event IDs, not ordering between different events, and subscriber pricing trusts this local status. This occurs with matched subscription IDs and does not depend on B68's unmatched-customer fallback.

B56.title: P1 candidate — Concurrent manager attendance corrections can violate final clock-in/out order and distort timesheet work minutes

checks.reason: The locking query does not lock only the targeted event: select_for_update() without an of restriction also locks rows joined through select_related, including the shared session and pharmacy. On PostgreSQL, corrections to different events in the same session therefore cannot both proceed through chronology validation concurrently. The waiting transaction reads the opposing correction after acquiring the shared lock, and the chronology check rejects the proposed inversion.

B58.title: P1 conditional — Internal draft becomes pharmacy-visible when worker sets paid status without delivery

checks.reason: The invoice owner can mark an undelivered internal draft paid, and both the received-invoice query and document visibility helper then expose it to the pharmacy. This also exposes an unsent correction as the current revision. The impact is narrower than payment approval or settlement: no Payment is created, review status remains separate, and visibility stays within the correct pharmacy.

B60.title: P1 concurrency candidate — Two overlapping distinct PENDING leave requests can both be approved

checks.reason: Overlapping pending requests can be created, and approval locks only the individual leave row. Concurrent approvals of distinct rows can both pass the approved-overlap query before either commits; no database exclusion constraint prevents this. This is an administrative consistency bug, but the timesheet summary merges overlapping leave intervals, so duplicate paid minutes are not established.

B62.title: P1 candidate — A Region Admin with communication-only privileges can manage shift operations despite missing roster capability

checks.reason: An assigned Region Admin at COMMUNICATION_MANAGER level can create shifts and description templates because the management helper ignores admin_level. Existing-shift mutations additionally depend on queryset visibility, so unrestricted mutation of every assigned pharmacy shift is not established. The claimed workforce contrast is inaccurate: central Region Admin capabilities also add MANAGE_ROSTER regardless of the selected level, while the cited roster-denial tests cover PharmacyAdmin users.

B64.title: P1 information-handling candidate — Kiosk one-time secrets are persisted to durable notifications and broadcast to app/WebSocket/device push

checks.reason: Pairing codes and PIN setup OTPs are stored verbatim in notification bodies and payloads, then forwarded without redaction to WebSocket subscribers and active Expo tokens. The pairing test explicitly requires this behavior. Delivery targets the intended user, REST reads are user-scoped, and credential expiry still prevents later redemption; changing notification delivery or retention therefore requires a policy decision.

B41.title: P1 candidate — Pending/rejected membership can be treated as private shift audience

checks.reason: Private shift listing, detail access and announcement recipients check active membership without requiring ACCEPTED status. Normal invitations start inactive, but an authorized manager can PATCH a pending membership active without changing its status; status is independently writable as well. This makes the reported state reachable through the API, and serializer output does not add an acceptance guard.

B44.title: P1 candidate — Invalid identity tab submission may erase or detach existing verified ID evidence

checks.reason: A request that reaches identity submission validation can already have deleted replaced or cleared files, saved document changes, and reset verification before returning 400. The reference check protects other profiles' files, but deliberately excludes the profile being edited. This affects the caller's explicitly edited evidence, and an existing test expressly expects draft edits to persist after submission refusal, so changing rollback or evidence-retention behavior requires a product decision.

B47.title: P1 candidate / owner role-policy decision: Organization email invitations immediately activate full administrative membership for an existing user

checks.reason: InviteOrgUserView.perform_create looks up an existing user by email. It then creates or updates their OrganizationMembership (role, admin_level, region, pharmacies) at once, before any email is sent. The model has no pending or accepted state, and OrganizationRolePermission and the org dashboard trust that row straight away, so access really is granted without acceptance. The inviter is still held to their own delegation scope by _enforce_org_delegation, so nobody gets more power than the inviter already has. The real gaps are consent and transparency, which makes this an owner policy choice (pharmacy-admin invites, by contrast, wait for acceptance), not a privilege escalation. test_region_delegation.py asserts this immediate behaviour on purpose.

B49.title: P1 candidate — Attachment/document upload type validation trusts client-declared MIME after failed magic-byte detection

checks.reason: validate_uploaded_file uses effective_type = sniffed_type or content_type. When the magic bytes don't match, the client-declared Content-Type decides, so b'NOT A PDF' named x.pdf with content_type application/pdf passes. Chat (both POST paths) and Hub attachments then store it. The filename extension is still limited to the allowed list, so the stored object keeps a .pdf/.docx/image extension. Browser XSS from this is not shown, which makes this a content-integrity or disguised-file risk (P2), not a P1. No test in the repo covers file_validation.

B51.title: P1 / potentially P0-impact candidate: Revoked pharmacy chat participant can send new messages through direct message endpoint after leaving the pharmacy

checks.reason: MessageViewSet.create does check only for a Participant row. But a post_save receiver on Membership (sync_membership_to_community_chat) deletes the user's Participant rows in that pharmacy's GROUP conversations whenever a save leaves the membership inactive, not ACCEPTED, or a non-staff employment type. That covers quit (LEFT), reject, the generic PATCH in perform_update, and the ProtectedError fallback in destroy. destroy itself deletes participations explicitly, and no queryset.update() on Membership skips the signal. A revoked member therefore has no Participant row and gets 403. Direct messages surviving after someone leaves is a separate policy question, not this finding.

B71.title: P1 user-flow reliability candidate: shift offer acceptance commits before notification errors can surface to the caller

checks.reason: accept commits the booking inside transaction.atomic, and ATOMIC_REQUESTS is not set. It then calls notify_shift_users and async_task outside any try/except. notify_users -> _broadcast does an uncaught channel-layer group_send, and async_task -> send_task raises if the Celery broker is down. An outage of Redis or the broker after commit therefore returns a 500 to the worker even though the booking is saved, and a retry gets 'Offer is not pending'. Data stays consistent and this only happens during an infrastructure outage, so P2. The codebase already has deliver_email_best_effort for exactly this pattern.
